raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Corn Dip
raw_recipe.description: A can of Mexican-style corn adds texture, taste and color to this standard Southwestern dip.
raw_recipe.name: Spicy Corn Dip

recipeInstructions.text: In a medium bowl, mix together sour cream, mayonnaise, corn, green onions, jalapeno chile peppers, green chile peppers and cheese. Ready to serve!

review.reviewBody:
I crave this dip all the time now. Some things I've learned about making it-
Drain, drain, drain anything that is liquidly (especially the corn). The first time I made this I dumped everything in a bowl, and it was kinda runny. But the 2nd time I made it I drained the corn and it made such a huge difference. 
Also, when dealing with the spicey aspects of the dip, I used 8oz of chilies instead 7, I put the peppers and the green onions together in a food processor and spooned in the "perfect" amount-- I added more onions and peppers to the food processor than recommended so that way I wasn't limited, nor was I adding too much. I've made this twice and everyone loves it and I plan to make it many many more times!

This dip was a hit at my 4th Party. I drained the corn and chili's. Used the jalapeno's in a jar and baked it till it was bubbling. Used frito's and chips for dipping. Everyone wanted the recipe.

Enjoy!

I liked this and most people at the party loved it too. I served it cold initially. My bf, who will eat anything passed on it all together though. Says it was too heavy. With the leftovers...I spread it out in a casserole dish, sprinkled Tony Chacheres on top and then a layer of cheddar cheese. Baked it at 350 until the cheese was melted and bubbly. I

03.03.17 ~ DRAIN the corn! This was a nice dip to take in to a lunch carry-in for the nurses' birthday. It was very quick to put together and packed with flavor. I've made dips similar to this before and knew that you needed to DRAIN the corn. If not, your dip will be very runny. We also enjoy this heated up. 
Cold or warm, it makes for a nice change for a get together.

Absolutely loved this dip! I skipped on the jalapenos, only did 1 green onion, we used leftover corn-on-the-cob (cut off the cob!), and fiesta blend shredded cheese. Also, added seasoned salt & pepper, Freddy's Fry Seasoning, and some cayenne pepper. You won't regret making this!

I added mozzarella cheese on top before baking or placing in a crockpot on low for 1 &1/2 hours stirring often. I used sour cream and chives, garlic and onion powders versus raw onion--no mayo. Teenager and adults enjoyed! Served with scoops and raw green and red pepper strips. A Christmas favorite appetizer!

Whenever I make this, I eat and eat until I can't chew any more. It's hard to stop. Definitely refrigerate this overnight because that's when the magic happens and the flavors blend together and the peppers heat everything up. I like it a little hotter so I don't remove the seeds from the jalepenos and I also add 3 habaneros and their seeds. Three of each seems to be the best for most people I've made this for. When it's just for me, I add 5 habaneros and it's not inferno-hot, but just enough to make your mouth tingle for a while. This makes about 7 cups of dip and you'll need two 15oz bags of Fritos Scoops to go with it. Super easy, super fast, super yummy!

I made it the first time as written and it really didn't do much for me. I didn't like the flavor of the canned corn as it tasted soggy and overcooked to me. The second time I used frozen corn that I thawed and drained and heated the dip in the oven for about 30 minutes. I also used more jalapenos since we like things with more heat and we all liked it much better the second time around.
I’ve made this so many times! Agreed with the drain the corn and it’s perfect! Always served it cold but maybe try it hot next!!
I make this often. I use half the amount of sour cream and mayo, and twice as much cheese. And like others have said, it's really important to drain the veggies well. I add just a bit of cumin. YUM!
so good. we do it in a casserole dish and cook it until the cheese bubbles. soooooo good.
Great dip! Took it to my church outing, it was a hit. I wouldn’t change a thing, other than making it more spicy.
Always a hit for potlucks! Make sure you leave the seeds in so it’s actually spicy!
I made as written and next time I added a few shakes of cumin and chili powder and a pinch of salt.
My wife always bought this kind of dip at the grocery store. I thought I would surprise her with something homemade. She absolutely loved this dip!
Easy , delicious and gluten free. Everyone loved it at our party!

I love this dip, it is Ah-Mazing! The recipe that I have calls for a couple of dashes of hot sauce (I used Siracha) and a sprinkle of Cavender's seasoning to taste. I think these little tweaks make it even better. There is never any left when I take this to a party and it is my most requested recipe. We love it!
Great recipe! I added a little extra shredded cheese just because I could. I'd highly recommend this for a crowd pleaser!
I make this for every family gathering and everyone raves about! I use can jalapenos and always let it chill in the fridge for at least 6 hours. ?? this recipe is amazing!!
